candidates.rationale: The procedure explicitly constructs a trellis and distinguishes admissible transitions and emissions. A compact illustrative trellis could make the algorithm’s state/time structure immediately legible.
candidates.draw_or_check: Show layers t=1,...,T with each state s in S; initial weights alpha_y(s)=pi(s)B(s,y_1); edges r at t-1 to s at t only if A(r,s)>0 and B(s,y_t)>0, labeled w_t(r,s); terminal weight beta_y(s)=1. Distinguish an absent zero-factor edge.

candidates.rationale: The nearest-center rule and tie-breaking cell definition are precise but dense; an optional one-dimensional schematic could make the cells and boundary tie convention easier to parse.
candidates.draw_or_check: Place ordered centers c_1<...<c_k on a real line; mark midpoint boundaries, assign each boundary to the smaller index, and show cells C_i intersected with X. Note that this illustrates only the nearest-center rule, not every measurable quantizer or compander partition.
